steps.what: Instruct students through lectures, discussions and demonstrations

tasks.design: Keep live instruction with the teacher. Existing materials from the {DOCS} may support demonstrations, but software does not replace the teacher's contact time in this boundary.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work is responsive instruction rather than repeated data entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital teaching materials can support delivery without shortening it.
tasks.still_hard: Spotting confusion while keeping a mixed group engaged.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher notices hesitation, changes pace and demonstrates safely.
tasks.altitude: Teaching time and decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Access needs and safe demonstration setup

evidence.claim: Live group instruction requires responsive teaching; this design claims no reduction in contact time.

assumptions: Boundary is lesson delivery; material preparation belongs to its own task and is not counted here.
Learner responses are produced directly by students during instruction. No structured input or automated action is introduced.
Native presentation settings can be used as already available; no custom build or ongoing new upkeep is proposed, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Class size, subject and access needs
research_questions: Which parts of a session require closer individual attention?

incremental.description: No change to delivery or software upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100; gross and net are zero. Digital aids do not remove live teaching in either individual or group sessions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Adapt methods and materials to learners

steps.what: Identify students' needs and choose changes to teaching methods
Adapt instructional materials to the chosen needs and interests

loop.purpose: Rewrite a selected passage at a suitable level
loop.input: Teacher brief and approved source passage
loop.check: Teacher checks factual meaning, instructions, accessibility and suitability against the original and brief
loop.stop: One draft and one revision, then teacher completes manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Changing wording without changing meaning needs semantic judgement; an existing suitable version is reused first

steps.what: Check adapted materials and try the teaching methods with students

tasks.design: Reuse suitable versions in the {DOCS} before drafting anything. A bounded writing aid proposes a passage from the teacher's source and brief; the teacher checks it and decides how to use it with students.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rewriting a passage takes time even after the teacher has chosen the adaptation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing lesson editors offer text rewriting at different levels.
tasks.still_hard: A readable passage may still be unsuitable for a particular learner or practical activity.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher understands learner confidence and tests whether an adaptation helps.
tasks.altitude: Some wording work falls away; the teacher retains all adaptation decisions and contact time.

reach.task: Review a small set of reusable accessible learning materials
reach.learn: Accessibility checking and source version control

evidence.claim: LessonUp offers AI text rewriting at another difficulty, summaries and translation; this supports a drafting capability, not measured savings for self-enrichment teachers.
The proposed time split and bounded rewriting savings are unmeasured scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary includes deciding, rewriting and testing an adaptation; general lesson delivery is counted separately.
Teacher produces the brief in s1: learning aim, intended level, interests, access constraints and changes to avoid. All capture time stays in the retained 40 percent.
Teacher selects the source passage and its version in s2; selection, checking and manual fallback are within its retained 21 hours. Do not infer needs from sensitive learner records.
Test native lesson-editor rewriting and reuse first. If access or rights are missing, edit manually.
Source content is supplied by the teacher from existing authorised materials; no new external collection is assumed.
unknowns: Share of materials requiring wording changes
research_questions: Does teacher-checked rewriting preserve instructions and meaning while reducing total preparation time?

already_counted.description: Source selection, checking the rewrite and manual exception editing
Final suitability decision and learner trial

incremental.description: Maintain a small approved source and brief collection

approvals.approved_version: Exact adapted passage and teaching-use plan checked at the start of s3; any wording or intended-use change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=40+35*0.60+25=86. Gross 14, less 1 upkeep gives net 13. Low is manual editing or no suitable rewriting work; high assumes the 35-hour wording slice is present and teacher review fits the retained time. Live decisions and trial time do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Encourage students to explore learning opportunities and persevere with challenging tasks

tasks.design: Retain the personal conversation and support during challenging work. A course list in the {DOCS} can be consulted as today, without claiming a reduction in encouragement time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Motivation depends on the learner and the relationship.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital course information is available, but it does not perform this conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing a useful challenge from an inaccessible or discouraging task.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher offers credible encouragement informed by observed effort.
tasks.altitude: The teacher retains the same coaching responsibilities.

reach.learn: Local course requirements and inclusive guidance

evidence.claim: Encouragement is relational work; no saving is assigned to replacing the teacher's conversation.

assumptions: Boundary is encouragement during learning, not course administration or catalogue maintenance.
Students produce goals and express concerns in the conversation; the teacher uses existing course information. There is no machine action requiring a structured record.
No additional capture, custom code or upkeep is introduced; zero incremental work follows from the unchanged design. Existing native resources remain optional.
unknowns: Learner goals and reasons for disengagement
research_questions: What forms of encouragement do learners find useful when work becomes difficult?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, incremental=0. Both routine encouragement and sensitive conversations retain their time; no administrative baseline is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Observe students to determine abilities, interests, qualifications and limitations

tasks.design: Keep observation and interpretation with the teacher. If existing notes are consulted in the {DOCS}, this remains part of the same human assessment rather than a new scoring system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Individual characteristics are contextual and cannot be inferred reliably from a few standard fields.
tasks.enabler_now: No technical change is needed for this boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Avoiding assumptions about a learner's ability from one performance.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher observes over time and asks the learner for context.
tasks.altitude: Observation responsibilities and decision rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Discuss accessible ways for learners to demonstrate understanding
reach.learn: Observation bias and inclusive assessment methods

evidence.claim: Direct contextual observation remains human work in this design; there is no proposed automated learner assessment.

assumptions: Boundary is observation and interpretation, not separately assigned progress-report writing.
Learners produce practice and explanations during teaching. No structured characteristics profile is assumed to exist or produced for automation.
Existing native notes may support the teacher; no new recording requirement, software build or upkeep is introduced, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Observation setting and individual access needs
research_questions: How does the teacher check an initial impression with the learner before changing instruction?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100. No machine assessment or extra clerical baseline is assumed; net saving is zero across routine and complex observations.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain live teaching and observation while reducing some checked wording work.
reach: Review reusable accessible materials with an instructional coordinator
skills_to_grow: Check rewritten instructions for meaning and accessibility
role.ambitious_version: Use a small reusable materials collection to support varied learner needs while keeping teaching decisions personal.
